summary: Seasonal fire lookout at Bernard Peak above Lake Pend Oreille: 1918 platform tower, 40-foot L-4 from 1948, destroyed in 1976; trails and a drivable road reach the summit.

facts.design: 40-foot treated timber L-4 tower with cab, built in 1948 about 500 feet north of the summit
facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1976. WillhiteWeb photographs a footing dated 8/8/63 and Idaho Fire Lookouts reports an engraved piece of concrete; no tower stands
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Kaniksu National Forest per firelookout.com)

staffing.status: seasonal; named lookouts from 1950 to 1970 in the sources; none listed after 1970

access.note: WillhiteWeb describes hiking trails from Farragut State Park and says the summit should be drivable if no gates or trees block the road. No closure rule was found, and gate status is not confirmed

visit.trail_note: No tower stands to climb. WillhiteWeb gives the hike as eight miles one way and says the Scout Trail starts at Farragut State Park

corrections.why: Firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts, Rex's page (quoting Kresek) and WillhiteWeb all date the 20-foot platform tower to 1918; only the register's Built field gives 1919. Medium confidence; the register's date is kept in resolved_conflicts.
6.1 m is the 20-foot 1918 platform tower. The tower standing until 1976 was a 40-foot L-4 tower, per the register, firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts and WillhiteWeb.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register's Built field gives 1919 and a pole tower; four other sites give a 20-foot platform tower in 1918. The correction uses 1918 and the story reports both.
Rex's page, quoting Kresek, gives 35 feet; the register, firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts and WillhiteWeb give 40 feet. The record uses 40 feet (12.2 m). The story reports the 35-foot figure.

The register gives 5,049 ft (1,539 m), which matches the brief's 1538.9 m. Idaho Fire Lookouts and WillhiteWeb give 5,156 ft. No source explains the gap; the brief's figure is kept and the difference is not in the story.
The register and Idaho Fire Lookouts' tower page name Chad Kinzel; firelookout.com names Charles Kinzel. The story uses Chad Kinzel, as the register does, and notes the other name.

The register says U.S. Forest Service; firelookout.com gives Kaniksu National Forest; Idaho Fire Lookouts gives Coeur d'Alene National Forest. The record keeps U.S. Forest Service and names Kaniksu from firelookout.com. The story does not name the forest.

notes_for_editor: Two corrections are proposed: the build year (1918 per four sites, not 1919) and the height (12.2 m for the 40-foot L-4 standing until 1976, not the 20-foot platform tower's 6.1 m). Access is marked public on the strength of the Farragut State Park trail routes and WillhiteWeb's drivable-summit remark; no closure or gate rule was found, so confirm before publishing. The 1967 Kinzel first name differs between sources. The FFA Historian's Facebook story about 1967 appeared in search results only and was neither read nor quoted. The Chad Kinzel story linked from Idaho Fire Lookouts was not followed. Photo credits (Fire Lookout Museum, Dave Bula collection, National Archives) come without image URLs, so none added.
